topIssues.title: [PCD] Default-`X` benchmarking
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: `X` (the offset between the chosen L1 anchor's timestamp and the committed L2 `genesis_time`) must be large enough that `genesis_time` is still in the future when `OPCM.deploy()` is mined; otherwise `op-node` will produce empty filler blocks at L2 block time to fill the gap. Measure end-to-end runtime of the off-chain portion of the pipeline (anchor selection through prestate generation) against a real prestate builder, repeated enough times to get a stable result. Propose a default `X`.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: run L1 and L2 test suites on different EVM versions
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
Testing branch for Glamsterdam (Amsterdam EVM) readiness — draft to exercise CI.

Amsterdam activates on L1 only, so `just test` now partitions its file list and runs everything outside `test/L2` against the Amsterdam EVM while `test/L2` stays on the default. CI calls `just test` / `just test-rerun` instead of forge directly, and installs a source-built forge at foundry commit f7a1468 (Amsterdam support was reverted upstream; the build is cached by commit).

Expected red: the Amsterdam pass fails on the known blockers (OPCM deploy gas, messenger baseGas) documented in the branch.

topPRs.title: op-reth: meter PostExec structural validation failures
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds a reason-labelled execution-client counter for PostExec block-level structural validation failures:

`optimism_post_exec.validation_failures{reason="..."}`

The bounded reason labels cover:

- `invalid_encoding_or_schema`
- `sdm_inactive`
- `multiple_transactions`
- `not_last`
- `block_number_mismatch`

The counter is recorded when op-reth rejects malformed PostExec structure while converting an Engine API payload, preparing block execution, or rebuilding derived payload attributes.

This addresses the observability question raised in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/388#discussion_r3829898758.

## Tests

- `cd rust && just fmt-check`
- `cd rust && cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-node --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cd rust && cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-node --lib`
- `cd rust && cargo check -p reth-optimism-evm --no-default-features`

## Review

The automated Rust review agent was unavailable in this harness; the change was manually reviewed against `docs/ai/rust-dev.md`.

topPRs.title: alloy-op-evm: regression-test dropped-tx SDM policy-touch rollback
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
## Overview

Adds a regression test for the SDM producer-policy "Leak B" residual and a doc-comment guard on the raw execution path. **Test-only + doc — no production behavior change.**

Leak B: in Produce mode, a dropped state-invalid tx still records its fee-vault touches on the `transact_raw` error path (`note_post_exec_account_touch` runs before the error is surfaced). This is *neutralized today* — `execute_transaction_with_commit_condition` snapshots the producer policy in Produce mode and restores it on `Err` — but that neutralization was unpinned for this specific path:

- the existing `warm_set_leak` tests use a stateless policy (`FixedRefundPolicy`) and assert on gas, so they cannot observe a policy-map leak;
- `execution_error_restores_refund_policy_snapshot` mutates policy state in `begin_tx` (pre-execution), not via `note_account_touch` (the error-path call Leak B rides).

Not an active bug: the only direct caller of `execute_transaction_without_commit` is a happy-path test; every production path (op-reth build loop, op-rbuilder, premium's producer) routes through the wrapper, and the public policy is stateless.

## Changes

- **Test** (`block/tests/structural_tests.rs`): a stateful `FeeVaultTouchPolicy` whose only mutation is in `note_account_touch`, plus `dropped_nonce_too_low_tx_...` and `dropped_eip3607_tx_...` cases asserting a dropped tx leaves the policy's block-scoped set empty, via the production `execute_transaction` path.
- **Doc** (`block/mod.rs`): note that `execute_transaction_without_commit` does not roll back producer-policy state, so a fallible tx must go through `execute_transaction_with_commit_condition`. This is what guards against a future direct raw-path caller — the actual residual.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --package alloy-op-evm` — 72 passed.
- **Non-vacuity**: both new tests fail with `a dropped failing tx left fee-vault touches in the producer policy` when the wrapper's `Err`-branch restore is temporarily removed (reverted after).
- `just fmt-fix`, `cargo clippy --package alloy-op-evm --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `just check-no-std` — clean.

## Note

This makes #21800 redundant: its rejected-candidate rollback already landed via #21359, and develop's wrapper restores on both execution error and commit-decline. #21800 can be closed as superseded (it also still edits the pre-#22289 `block/tests.rs`).

v0.69.0 / 2026-06-17

Security / behavior changes

  • config: credentials are no longer forwarded across cross-host redirects. When FollowRedirects is enabled, the HTTP client now strips Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and other sensitive headers, and skips basic-auth, bearer-token and OAuth2 credentials, when a redirect points to a different host. This aligns with Go's net/http behavior. Callers that relied on credentials being sent to a redirect target on another host will need to target that host directly. #901 #920 #921
  • config: LoadHTTPConfigFile now resolves relative file paths (e.g. *_file credentials, http_headers files) against the config file's own directory instead of its parent directory. Configs that worked around the old behavior by prefixing paths with the config's directory name must drop that prefix. #925

Bugfixes

  • expfmt: fix nil pointer panic when parsing empty braces {}. #922
  • model: fix Time.UnmarshalJSON for larger negative numbers. #918

Performance

Internal

  • Synchronize common files from prometheus/prometheus. #917
  • Modernize Go. #919
